key_insight: Adversarial Heuristic Learning lets fixed-weight AI agents improve game policies and supporting software by iteratively analyzing competition experience, but success remains uneven across complex games.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how agentic systems can be used as an automated software-improvement loop for game-playing code under realistic budget constraints, without retraining model weights.
method: Define AHL as heuristic learning driven by AI agents that read rules, pick opponents, study replays, and revise executable game programs.
Benchmark on AAArena: 12 adversarial games and 1,920 archived human programs with competition-style rankings and fixed match/evaluation budgets.
Test multiple model/harness setups to see whether agentic revision improves ladder performance and strategy quality.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, Opus5.5 with Claude Code achieved 6 gold medals, while no evaluated configuration topped the remaining 6 human ladders; performance was weaker in games with more complex rules.
watch_item: Results depend heavily on rule comprehension and long-horizon strategy implementation, so gains may not transfer reliably to more complex or less well-specified games.
paper_title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition
